statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low and well below the block threshold, while Stress stays elevated ahead of the stacked 26 August U.S. data release and the NVIDIA report that follows it.
recommendation: The retracement from the session high has deepened rather than failed: NQ trades roughly 216 points below the 29,426 high and in the lower part of the 29,157-29,426 range, with VIX down 6.0%, crude off more than 3% and Treasury yields easing. That describes functioning rather than failing mean reversion, and the mapped state remains EA_ON. A narrow danger window is marked from the 26 August 12:30Z Core PCE, GDP and durable-goods release through the first hours of U.S. cash trade, where conditional Tail is projected to reach the watch band without crossing the block threshold.
headline: Nasdaq-100 keeps a chip-led gain but drifts further off its high; risk stays concentrated on tomorrow's PCE, GDP and NVIDIA stack
body: NQ futures trade near 29,210, about +0.36% on the session, having given back roughly 216 points from the 29,426 session high and now sitting in the lower part of the 29,157-29,426 range. That deepening retracement is the central structural observation: the tape keeps an upward bias but is clearly two-sided, and mean reversion is working rather than failing. Cross-assets support that read instead of amplifying it. VIX is 14.89, down 6.0% with a 14.77-15.95 range; WTI has fallen about 3.3% to $82.22 and Brent about 4.0% to $88.51 as U.S. measures against Iran were read as less disruptive than markets had braced for; and the 10-year Treasury yield has eased roughly 5bp to 4.65% against the 4.75% high set on 21 August, with the 2-year at 4.21%. Leadership is narrow and semiconductor-led, with six of seven tracked chip names higher on the latest session and AMD up more than 4%, while the eight tracked megacaps are split four-four. Macro news flow today was soft rather than destabilising: Conference Board consumer confidence fell to 89.4 against a 90.2 consensus, a seven-month low, and July new home sales dropped 10.5% to 607K. Canada announced dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs on about $20 billion of U.S. goods effective 8 September, which U.S. equities largely absorbed. None of the amplifiers that would justify a materially higher Tail are present: there is no persistent one-way structure, no sequence of failed retracements, no holding near a session extreme, and no aligned yields-VIX-oil-breadth configuration. Risk on this horizon is instead concentrated in a narrow forward window on 26 August, when Core PCE, the GDP second estimate and July durable goods print together at 12:30Z and post-release repricing overlaps the 13:30Z cash open, with NVIDIA results following after the close.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 hours the assessment never left the low-to-watch Tail band. Tail sat between 7 and 12 through the 24 August U.S. evening and the Asian session under normal and mixed modes, then built steadily from 04:00Z on 25 August as a trend-up bias developed, reaching the 20-21 watch band between 09:00Z and 12:00Z across the European morning and the U.S. pre-market. From 13:00Z the mode reverted to mixed and Tail eased through 17, 16 and 14 to 13 by 17:00Z as the U.S. cash session turned two-sided and the move off the session high extended. Stress held between 42 and 51 throughout and Confidence stayed high, between 84 and 88.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours divide into three phases. Through the remainder of the 25 August U.S. session, conditional Tail drifts up from 12 to a session peak of 15 across power hour and the 20:00Z cash close, which coincides with a scheduled Fed Barkin speech, then falls back once cash trading ends. The overnight Asian and early European stretch is projected at the low end, Tail 9 to 14, with no scheduled U.S. macro and a benign cross-asset backdrop assumed to persist while Confidence decays with evidence age. Risk then builds into 26 August: conditional Tail reaches 23 for the 12:00Z hour containing the stacked Core PCE, GDP second estimate and durable-goods release, and peaks at 24 for the 13:00Z hour where post-release repricing overlaps the U.S. cash open. That overlap is the single configuration on this horizon most capable of producing a poorly retraced path, and it stays below the block threshold, mapping to WATCH rather than a block state. Tail then normalises through the 26 August afternoon as attention rotates to the NVIDIA report due after the cash close, which falls outside this horizon.
